Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

entertainment noun

also entertain (amuse), amusement, amusements, pastime, the entertainment industry, shows, entertainer

classical

Plin. Ep. 9.17.4: aliēnīs oblectātiōnibus
Cic. Lael. 103: requiēs plēna oblectātiōnis (Lewis & Short)

oblectātiō, oblectātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

amusement, entertainment, delight

A favourite word of Cicero’s (Lewis & Short): whatever pleasantly fills the time. Pliny uses the plural of the turns put on at dinner, readers, musicians, clowns.

Other words

  • oblectāmentum, oblectāmentī n. — an amusement, a pastime

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 52: requiēs oblectāmentumque senectūtis (Lewis & Short)

    The thing that amuses, where oblectātiō is the amusing.

  • spectācula, spectāculōrum n. pl. — shows, public entertainments

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. spectāculum

    Shows to watch: games, plays, and now films and television.

  • ācroāma, ācroāmatis n. — an entertainment at dinner (music or reading); an entertainer

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Arch. 20 (Lewis & Short); Plin. Ep. 6.31.13 (Lewis & Short)

    Greek, “something heard”: the music or reading that entertained guests at table, and the performer who gave it (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • dēmus igitur aliēnīs oblectātiōnibus veniam, ut nostrīs impetrēmus

    let us then forgive other people their entertainments, so that ours may be forgivenPlin. Ep. 9.17.4

See also fun, pleasure, receive, programme.
